description: Minimum vertex coloring on deterministic benchmark graphs, verified by recomputing conflict-freeness from the emitted assignment and compared against DSATUR and TabuCol baselines.

problem_shape.objective: Minimize the number of colors in a proper vertex coloring (no edge joins two same-colored vertices).
problem_shape.input_representation: An undirected graph as an adjacency list, generated deterministically from a named instance (random G(n,p), queen graphs, planted k-partite).
constraints: The coloring must be proper: zero conflicting edges when recomputed from the emitted assignment.
Color count is recomputed from the assignment, never taken from the solver's report.
Stochastic methods must report across the declared fixed seeds with a fixed iteration budget.
failure_modes: Candidate beats greedy or DSATUR but loses to TabuCol at the same iteration budget.
Candidate reports a color count without a proper coloring behind it.
Candidate tuned on one instance family (e.g. G(n,0.5)) that regresses on queen or planted instances.
Wall-clock advantage from a lower-level language mistaken for an algorithmic win.

recommended_problem_template: Find proper vertex colorings of benchmark graphs using fewer colors than descending-k TabuCol seeded from DSATUR at an equal iteration budget, across fixed seeds and all instance families.
